---
title: "Virus RPKMF and Genome Copies Correlation Analysis"
output:
  pdf_document: default
  html_notebook: default
---

```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(data.table)
library(dplyr)
library(ggpubr)
library(rprojroot)
library(eoffice) # Load eoffice library for PPTX output

# Read the file path of the virus data
virus_data_file <- sprintf("%s/data/viru_RPKMF_genome_copies.tsv", find_rstudio_root_file())

# Load virus RPKMF and genome copies data
virus_data <- fread(virus_data_file, sep = "\t", header = TRUE)

# No log transformation, use the original values directly

# Correlation plot with facet_wrap for different viruses
correlation_plot <- ggscatter(
  virus_data, x = "RPKMF", y = "genome_copies",
  add = "reg.line", conf.int = TRUE,
  cor.coef = TRUE, cor.method = "pearson", cor.p = TRUE,
  cor.coef.size = 5, 
  color = "#1F77B4"
) +
  facet_wrap(~ virus, scales = "free", ncol = 2) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_text(size = 12), 
    axis.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "top",
    plot.margin = unit(c(0.5, 1.5, 0.5, 0.5), "cm") 
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(name = "RPKMF") +
  scale_y_continuous(name = "Genome Copies")

# Save the correlation plot as a PDF file
ggsave(sprintf("%s/charts/Virus_RPKMF_GenomeCopies_Correlation_facet.pdf", find_rstudio_root_file()), correlation_plot, width = 8, height = 8)

# Save the correlation plot as a PPTX file
pptx_filename <- sprintf("%s/charts/Virus_RPKMF_GenomeCopies_Correlation_facet.pptx", find_rstudio_root_file())
topptx(correlation_plot, filename = pptx_filename, height = 8, width = 8)
```
